tool.name: cve_intel_search
tool.description:
Query Perplexity for fresh CVE intelligence on a specific `(tech, version)` pair. Augments `cve_lookup` (#61, OSV-backed) with web-indexed content — vendor advisories not yet in OSV, in-the-wild exploitation reports, recent PoCs.
Why this complements `cve_lookup`: - OSV.dev lags vendor advisories by hours-to-days. A 0-day disclosed Tuesday morning shows up in Perplexity's web-indexed corpus before OSV picks it up. - Vendor advisories that aren't formally CVE-numbered (GHSA / RHSA / vendor security bulletins) appear in Perplexity but may not show up in OSV. - "In the wild" exploitation reports (KEV-adjacent) come up in Perplexity even when KEV hasn't yet listed the CVE.
Auth: `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` env var (the same key gating the existing `web_search` tool). Without it, returns `success=False` with a clear error so the agent knows to fall back to `cve_lookup` only.
Methodology: 1. Build a structured prompt: "List all publicly-disclosed CVEs affecting ` ` as of ``. For each: CVE ID, severity, summary, exploit PoC URL, KEV status, fixed version. Don't make up CVE IDs." 2. POST to `https://api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions` with the `sonar-pro` model (better quality + citations than `sonar`). 3. Extract CVE IDs from the response content via `CVE-\d{4}-\d{4,}` regex (case-insensitive, deduped, sorted, capped at 50). 4. Capture Perplexity-supplied `citations[]` + URLs found inline in the response body.
The tool is **display-only** — does NOT emit findings. Perplexity output is LLM-generated and may include hallucinated CVE IDs. The agent's workflow: 1. `fingerprint_tech_stack` detects `(tech, version)`. 2. `cve_lookup` queries OSV (authoritative) for known CVEs. 3. `cve_intel_search` (this tool) queries Perplexity for FRESH intel. 4. The agent compares: any CVE mentioned by Perplexity but not OSV gets a follow-up `cve_lookup` query (in case OSV was stale) OR is flagged for human review.
Cache: per-(tech, version, model) JSON cache under `~/.strix/cve_intel_cache/`, 12-hour TTL. Stale-cache served on network failure (fail-open with `error` populated). Disable with `STRIX_CVE_INTEL_NO_CACHE=1`.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to the Perplexity request. `--exclude-path` doesn't apply (URL is api.perplexity.ai, not the customer's domain).

parameter.name: tech
parameter.description: Software / framework name (e.g. `Apache`, `Log4j`, `OpenSSL`). Free-text — Perplexity does its own fuzzy matching. Pair with the version detected by `fingerprint_tech_stack`.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.description: Per-request timeout in seconds. Default 60 (Sonar queries take 10-30s; budget more than typical HTTP).

parameter.name: model
parameter.description: Perplexity model to use. Default `sonar-pro` (better quality + citations). Alternatives: `sonar` (faster + cheaper), `sonar-reasoning-pro` (deeper reasoning, slower).

returns.description:
{success, tech, version, model, queried_at, from_cache, cves: [CVE-XXXX-XXXX, ...], citations: [url, ...] (Perplexity-supplied), inline_urls: [url, ...] (URLs in content body), summary: , error?}.
The agent should: 1. Cross-reference each CVE in `cves[]` with `cve_lookup` to verify it's a real CVE (not hallucinated). 2. For CVEs not yet in OSV, treat as a candidate worth manual review. 3. Use `citations[]` + `inline_urls[]` to surface authoritative sources to the user.
